title: Count Evenly Stepped Stretches
statement:
A stretch is a contiguous subarray of at least three elements. It is evenly stepped if the difference between each element and the next is the same all the way through (the step may be zero or negative).

Given an integer array nums, return how many of its stretches are evenly stepped. Stretches at different positions count separately, even if their values match.

examples.why: [1, 3, 5], [3, 5, 7] and the whole [1, 3, 5, 7]. Overlapping and nested stretches all count.
[4, 4, 4] with step 0 and [4, 2, 0] with step −2. [4, 4, 4, 2] mixes two steps.
Doubling is not a constant step.

hints: Think about stretches that end exactly at index i. How do they relate to the ones ending at i − 1?
If nums[i] − nums[i−1] equals nums[i−1] − nums[i−2], every evenly stepped stretch ending at i − 1 extends by one element, plus one new stretch of length 3 appears.
Let end[i] be the count ending at i: end[i] = end[i−1] + 1 when the last two steps match, else 0. The answer is the sum of end[i].

explain.intuition:
Count stretches by where they end. A stretch ending at i is evenly stepped exactly when the stretch one shorter, ending at i − 1, is evenly stepped (or is just two elements) and the newest step matches the previous one.

So if the steps at i and i − 1 match, every stretch that ended at i − 1 grows by one, and the three elements i−2, i−1, i form one more. That gives end[i] = end[i − 1] + 1. A mismatch breaks every stretch, so end[i] = 0. Only the previous value is needed.
steps: For i from 2 to n − 1: if nums[i] − nums[i−1] === nums[i−1] − nums[i−2], set cur += 1; otherwise cur = 0.
pitfalls: Counting only maximal runs. A run of length L contains (L − 1)(L − 2) / 2 stretches, not one.
Forgetting to reset cur on a mismatch, which lets stretches leak across a break.
Treating a step of 0 as invalid. Equal values are evenly stepped.

solutions.title: Check every stretch
solutions.idea: For each start, extend while the step stays equal to the first step, counting each stretch of length ≥ 3.

solutions.title: Count stretches ending here
solutions.idea: end[i] = end[i − 1] + 1 when the last two steps match, else 0; sum them.

followups: Count evenly stepped subsequences (not necessarily contiguous) of length ≥ 3. What state does the DP need now?
Return the longest evenly stepped stretch instead of the count.
